method: A scheduled job reads official state election-office files, keeps U.S. Senate, governor, and U.S. House contests, and writes one JSON file. Pages poll that file. They do not call a winner unless the official file marks one. States without a confirmed machine-readable file are a link only.

states.name: California
states.resultsLabel: California Secretary of State — election results
states.cors: The media JSON files do not send Access-Control-Allow-Origin. The browser reads this site's copy. api.sos.ca.gov sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * for the same figures.
states.terms: The Secretary of State publishes a media index at https://media.sos.ca.gov/media/json-endpoints.csv that lists the JSON files for the November 3, 2026 statewide general election. Each file includes a statewide or districtwide total and county rows. This project copies the statewide or districtwide votes, the percent, and the precincts-reporting line. The candidate records do not include a winner flag, so no winner is shown. County rows are not added together.
states.updateCadence: The media JSON files are replaced as counties report. This project checks every 10 minutes while counting continues.

states.terms: The State Board publishes election-night results as a JSON file under er.ncsbe.gov and precinct files under dl.ncsbe.gov. The file's pct field is a proportion; this site shows that proportion as a percent (0.5086 becomes 50.86) and does not recompute it from the vote counts. The file has no winner flag, so no winner is shown. Totals are unofficial until the board certifies the election.
states.updateCadence: The State Board replaces the election-night file as counties report. On a general-election night that is many times an hour. This project checks every 10 minutes while counting continues.
